title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Twitter/X — Social Media Feed System (deep dive)
summary: Covers System Requirements, Visual Architecture, Real-World Examples.

sections.title: System Requirements
sections.body:
### Functional Requirements

1. Post tweets (280 chars, images, videos)
2. Follow/unfollow users
3. News feed (timeline) — see tweets from followed users
4. Search tweets
5. Like, retweet, reply
6. Trending topics

### Non-Functional Requirements

- 500M users, 200M DAU
- 500M tweets/day (~6000 tweets/second)
- Read-heavy: 100:1 read/write ratio
- Timeline generation < 200ms
- 99.99% availability

diagrams.title: Timeline fan-out: on write for most users, on read for celebrities
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  t["New tweet"] --> who{"Author has > 1M followers?"}
  who -->|"no"| fw["Fan-out on write: push tweet id into each follower's Redis timeline"]
  who -->|"yes"| fr["Store once; merge into timelines at read time"]
  rd["User opens home timeline"] --> pre["Read precomputed timeline from Redis"]
  pre --> merge["Merge in recent tweets from followed celebrities"]
  fw --> pre
  fr --> merge
  merge --> rank["Rank and return"]
diagrams.explain: Reads outnumber writes enormously, so timelines are precomputed: when you tweet, your tweet id is pushed into every follower's cached timeline (**fan-out on write**). That breaks for accounts with millions of followers, so their tweets are fetched and merged at read time (**fan-out on read**). The hybrid keeps reads fast without million-write storms.

sections.title: Visual Architecture
sections.body:
### High-Level Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      TWITTER SYSTEM DESIGN                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Clients                    API Gateway               Core Services
  ───────                    ───────────               ─────────────

  Mobile App ──┐            ┌──────────────┐
  Web App    ──┼──────────▶│   API GW     │
  3rd Party  ──┘  HTTPS     │  Rate Limit  │
                            │  Auth (JWT)  │
                            └──────┬───────┘
                                   │
          ┌────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
          ▼                        ▼                        ▼
  ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐
  │ Tweet Service│        │ Timeline Svc │        │ User Service │
  │              │        │              │        │              │
  │ Create tweet │        │ Home timeline│        │ Follow/      │
  │ Delete tweet │        │ User timeline│        │ Unfollow     │
  │ Like/Retweet │        │ Feed ranking │        │ Profile      │
  └──────┬───────┘        └──────┬───────┘        └──────┬───────┘
         │                       │                        │
         ▼                       ▼                        ▼
  ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐
  │  Tweet DB    │        │  Feed Cache  │        │  User DB     │
  │  (Cassandra) │        │  (Redis)     │        │  (PostgreSQL)│
  └──────────────┘        └──────────────┘        └──────────────┘
```

### Fan-out Strategy (Core Algorithm)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               TIMELINE GENERATION: FAN-OUT                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  APPROACH 1: Fan-out on Write (Push)
  ─────────────────────────────────
  User A posts tweet → Push to ALL followers' timelines

  User A (1000 followers) posts "Hello World"
       │
       ├──▶ Follower 1's timeline cache: [tweet_A, ...]
       ├──▶ Follower 2's timeline cache: [tweet_A, ...]
       ├──▶ Follower 3's timeline cache: [tweet_A, ...]
       └──▶ ... × 1000 writes

  ✓ Fast reads (pre-computed)
  ✗ Slow writes for celebs (millions of followers)
  ✗ Wasted work if followers are inactive

  APPROACH 2: Fan-out on Read (Pull)
  ──────────────────────────────────
  When user opens timeline → Fetch tweets from all followed users

  User B opens timeline
       │
       ├──▶ Fetch User X's latest tweets
       ├──▶ Fetch User Y's latest tweets
       ├──▶ Fetch User Z's latest tweets
       └──▶ Merge + Sort by time

  ✓ No write amplification
  ✗ Slow reads (query N users)
  ✗ Hard to rank/personalize

  APPROACH 3: HYBRID (Twitter's actual approach)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  Regular users → Fan-out on Write (push)
  Celebrities (>10K followers) → Fan-out on Read (pull)

  Timeline = Pre-computed cache + Real-time celebrity fetch
```

### Data Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TWEET POSTING FLOW                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  1. User posts tweet
     │
  2. ▼ Tweet Service validates, stores in Tweet DB
     │
  3. ▼ Publishes "TweetCreated" event to Kafka
     │
     ├──▶ 4a. Fan-out Service: Push to followers' Redis timelines
     │         (skip if celebrity — followers will pull)
     │
     ├──▶ 4b. Search Indexer: Index tweet in Elasticsearch
     │
     ├──▶ 4c. Notification Service: Notify @mentioned users
     │
     ├──▶ 4d. Media Service: Process images/videos (thumbnails, encoding)
     │
     └──▶ 4e. Analytics: Track tweet metrics, trending hashtags
```

sections.title: 5 Real-World Examples
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Core Twitter system: Tweet storage and fan-out timeline generation
- Simulates Cassandra tweet storage
- User follow relationships
- Hybrid fan-out timeline generation
- Pre-computed timelines (Redis in production)
- Trim to max size
- 1. Get pre-computed timeline (from fan-out)
- 2. Fetch celebrity tweets on-the-fly (fan-out on read)

**Defines:** `Tweet`, `TweetStore`, `SocialGraph`, `TimelineService`, `TweetSearchEngine`, `TrendingService`, `FeedItem`, `FeedRanker`, `NotificationType`, `Notification`

### Example 1: Tweet Service & Fan-out System

```python
"""
Core Twitter system: Tweet storage and fan-out timeline generation
"""
import time
import heapq
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Optional
import uuid

@dataclass
class Tweet:
    tweet_id: str
    user_id: str
    content: str
    timestamp: float
    likes: int = 0
    retweets: int = 0
    reply_to: str = ""
    media_urls: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

class TweetStore:
    """Simulates Cassandra tweet storage"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.tweets: Dict[str, Tweet] = {}
        self.user_tweets: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)

    def create(self, user_id: str, content: str, reply_to: str = "") -> Tweet:
        tweet = Tweet(
            tweet_id=f"t_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
            user_id=user_id,
            content=content[:280],
            timestamp=time.time(),
            reply_to=reply_to
        )
        self.tweets[tweet.tweet_id] = tweet
        self.user_tweets[user_id].append(tweet.tweet_id)
        return tweet

    def get_user_tweets(self, user_id: str, limit: int = 20) -> List[Tweet]:
        ids = self.user_tweets.get(user_id, [])[-limit:]
        return [self.tweets[tid] for tid in reversed(ids)]

class SocialGraph:
    """User follow relationships"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.followers: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
        self.following: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)

    def follow(self, user_id: str, target_id: str):
        self.following[user_id].add(target_id)
        self.followers[target_id].add(user_id)

    def get_followers(self, user_id: str) -> Set[str]:
        return self.followers.get(user_id, set())

    def get_following(self, user_id: str) -> Set[str]:
        return self.following.get(user_id, set())

    def is_celebrity(self, user_id: str, threshold: int = 10000) -> bool:
        return len(self.followers.get(user_id, set())) >= threshold

class TimelineService:
    """Hybrid fan-out timeline generation"""

    CELEBRITY_THRESHOLD = 5  # Low for demo (real: 10000+)

    def __init__(self, tweet_store: TweetStore, social_graph: SocialGraph):
        self.tweet_store = tweet_store
        self.social_graph = social_graph
        # Pre-computed timelines (Redis in production)
        self.timeline_cache: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)
        self.MAX_TIMELINE = 800

    def fan_out_tweet(self, tweet: Tweet):
        """Push tweet to followers' timelines (fan-out on write)"""
        is_celeb = self.social_graph.is_celebrity(
            tweet.user_id, self.CELEBRITY_THRESHOLD
        )

        if is_celeb:
            print(f"  Celebrity tweet by {tweet.user_id} — skipping fan-out (pull on read)")
            return

        followers = self.social_graph.get_followers(tweet.user_id)
        for follower_id in followers:
            timeline = self.timeline_cache[follower_id]
            timeline.append(tweet.tweet_id)
            # Trim to max size
            if len(timeline) > self.MAX_TIMELINE:
                self.timeline_cache[follower_id] = timeline[-self.MAX_TIMELINE:]

        print(f"  Fan-out: pushed to {len(followers)} follower timelines")

    def get_timeline(self, user_id: str, limit: int = 20) -> List[Tweet]:
        """Get user's home timeline (hybrid approach)"""
        # 1. Get pre-computed timeline (from fan-out)
        cached_ids = self.timeline_cache.get(user_id, [])[-limit:]

        # 2. Fetch celebrity tweets on-the-fly (fan-out on read)
        following = self.social_graph.get_following(user_id)
        celebrity_tweets = []
        for followed_id in following:
            if self.social_graph.is_celebrity(followed_id, self.CELEBRITY_THRESHOLD):
                celebrity_tweets.extend(
                    self.tweet_store.get_user_tweets(followed_id, limit=5)
                )

        # 3. Merge and sort
        all_tweets = []
        for tid in cached_ids:
            if tid in self.tweet_store.tweets:
                all_tweets.append(self.tweet_store.tweets[tid])
        all_tweets.extend(celebrity_tweets)

        # Sort by timestamp descending
        all_tweets.sort(key=lambda t: t.timestamp, reverse=True)
        return all_tweets[:limit]

# ─── Demo ───
store = TweetStore()
graph = SocialGraph()
timeline = TimelineService(store, graph)

# Users: alice (celebrity, 6+ followers), bob, carol (regular)
users = ["alice", "bob", "carol", "dave", "eve", "frank", "grace"]
for u in users[1:]:
    graph.follow(u, "alice")  # Everyone follows alice (celebrity)
graph.follow("alice", "bob")
graph.follow("alice", "carol")
graph.follow("carol", "bob")

# Post tweets
t1 = store.create("bob", "Hello from Bob! #python")
timeline.fan_out_tweet(t1)

t2 = store.create("alice", "Celebrity tweet from Alice! 🌟")
timeline.fan_out_tweet(t2)

t3 = store.create("carol", "Carol's thoughts on system design")
timeline.fan_out_tweet(t3)

# Get Alice's timeline
print("\n📱 Alice's timeline:")
for tweet in timeline.get_timeline("alice"):
    print(f"  @{tweet.user_id}: {tweet.content}")

print("\n📱 Bob's timeline:")
for tweet in timeline.get_timeline("bob"):
    print(f"  @{tweet.user_id}: {tweet.content}")
```

### Example 2: Search & Trending Topics

```python
"""
Twitter search engine and trending topics
"""
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import re
import time

class TweetSearchEngine:
    """Simulates Elasticsearch for tweet search"""

    def __init__(self):
        self.inverted_index: Dict[str, List] = defaultdict(list)
        self.hashtag_index: Dict[str, List] = defaultdict(list)
        self.tweets: Dict[str, dict] = {}

    def index_tweet(self, tweet_id: str, content: str,
                    user_id: str, timestamp: float):
        doc = {"tweet_id": tweet_id, "content": content,
               "user_id": user_id, "timestamp": timestamp}
        self.tweets[tweet_id] = doc

        # Tokenize and index
        words = re.findall(r'\w+', content.lower())
        for word in words:
            self.inverted_index[word].append(tweet_id)

        # Index hashtags
        hashtags = re.findall(r'#(\w+)', content.lower())
        for tag in hashtags:
            self.hashtag_index[tag].append((tweet_id, timestamp))

    def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 10) -> List[dict]:
        """Search tweets by keyword — ranked by recency"""
        terms = query.lower().split()
        if not terms:
            return []

        # Find tweets matching ALL terms
        result_sets = []
        for term in terms:
            result_sets.append(set(self.inverted_index.get(term, [])))

        if not result_sets:
            return []

        matching_ids = result_sets[0]
        for rs in result_sets[1:]:
            matching_ids &= rs

        # Sort by timestamp
        results = [self.tweets[tid] for tid in matching_ids if tid in self.tweets]
        results.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"], reverse=True)
        return results[:limit]

class TrendingService:
    """Real-time trending topics using sliding window"""

    def __init__(self, window_minutes: int = 60):
        self.window = window_minutes * 60
        self.hashtag_counts: List[tuple] = []  # (timestamp, hashtag)

    def record_hashtag(self, hashtag: str, timestamp: float = None):
        ts = timestamp or time.time()
        self.hashtag_counts.append((ts, hashtag.lower()))

    def get_trending(self, top_n: int = 10) -> List[dict]:
        """Get top trending hashtags in the time window"""
        now = time.time()
        cutoff = now - self.window

        # Count hashtags in window
        counter = Counter()
        valid = []
        for ts, tag in self.hashtag_counts:
            if ts >= cutoff:
                counter[tag] += 1
                valid.append((ts, tag))

        # Clean old entries
        self.hashtag_counts = valid

        return [
            {"hashtag": f"#{tag}", "count": count, "rank": i + 1}
            for i, (tag, count) in enumerate(counter.most_common(top_n))
        ]

# ─── Demo ───
search = TweetSearchEngine()
trending = TrendingService(window_minutes=60)

tweets_data = [
    ("t1", "alice", "Just shipped a new feature! #python #coding"),
    ("t2", "bob", "System design interview prep #coding #interview"),
    ("t3", "carol", "Love learning #python for data engineering #data"),
    ("t4", "dave", "Breaking: New AI model released #ai #tech"),
    ("t5", "eve", "Python vs Java for backend #python #java #coding"),
    ("t6", "frank", "#python is amazing for ML #ai #machinelearning"),
    ("t7", "grace", "Data pipeline best practices #data #python #coding"),
]

now = time.time()
for i, (tid, uid, content) in enumerate(tweets_data):
    search.index_tweet(tid, content, uid, now + i)
    for tag in re.findall(r'#(\w+)', content):
        trending.record_hashtag(tag, now + i)

# Search
print("Search 'python':")
for r in search.search("python"):
    print(f"  @{r['user_id']}: {r['content'][:50]}...")

print("\nSearch 'coding data':")
for r in search.search("coding data"):
    print(f"  @{r['user_id']}: {r['content'][:50]}...")

# Trending
print("\n🔥 Trending:")
for t in trending.get_trending(5):
    print(f"  {t['rank']}. {t['hashtag']} ({t['count']} tweets)")
```

### Example 3: Feed Ranking Algorithm

```python
"""
ML-inspired feed ranking for timeline personalization
"""
import math
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict

@dataclass
class FeedItem:
    tweet_id: str
    author_id: str
    content: str
    timestamp: float
    likes: int = 0
    retweets: int = 0
    replies: int = 0
    has_media: bool = False
    is_verified: bool = False

class FeedRanker:
    """
    Ranks tweets for timeline display using engagement signals
    Similar to real Twitter/X ranking
    """

    # Feature weights (in production: learned by ML)
    WEIGHTS = {
        "recency": 1.5,
        "engagement": 1.2,
        "user_affinity": 2.0,
        "content_quality": 0.8,
        "author_reputation": 1.0,
        "media_boost": 0.3,
    }

    def __init__(self):
        self.user_interactions: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        self.author_scores: Dict[str, float] = {}

    def set_user_affinity(self, user_id: str, author_id: str, score: float):
        """Track how much user engages with author"""
        self.user_interactions.setdefault(user_id, {})[author_id] = score

    def set_author_reputation(self, author_id: str, score: float):
        self.author_scores[author_id] = score

    def rank(self, user_id: str, items: List[FeedItem],
             limit: int = 20) -> List[tuple]:
        """Rank feed items for user"""
        scored = []
        for item in items:
            score = self._compute_score(user_id, item)
            scored.append((score, item))

        scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        return scored[:limit]

    def _compute_score(self, user_id: str, item: FeedItem) -> float:
        w = self.WEIGHTS

        # Recency: exponential decay (half-life = 6 hours)
        age_hours = (time.time() - item.timestamp) / 3600
        recency = math.exp(-0.115 * age_hours) * w["recency"]

        # Engagement: log-scaled
        engagement = math.log1p(
            item.likes + item.retweets * 2 + item.replies * 1.5
        ) * w["engagement"]

        # User affinity: past interaction with this author
        affinity = self.user_interactions.get(user_id, {}).get(
            item.author_id, 0.1
        ) * w["user_affinity"]

        # Author reputation
        reputation = self.author_scores.get(
            item.author_id, 0.5
        ) * w["author_reputation"]

        # Media boost
        media = (0.5 if item.has_media else 0) * w["media_boost"]

        # Verified boost
        verified = 0.2 if item.is_verified else 0

        total = recency + engagement + affinity + reputation + media + verified
        return round(total, 3)

# ─── Demo ───
ranker = FeedRanker()
ranker.set_user_affinity("user1", "alice", 0.9)
ranker.set_user_affinity("user1", "bob", 0.3)
ranker.set_author_reputation("alice", 0.95)
ranker.set_author_reputation("bob", 0.7)
ranker.set_author_reputation("news_bot", 0.8)

now = time.time()
items = [
    FeedItem("t1", "alice", "Amazing Python tricks", now - 3600, likes=150, retweets=30, has_media=True, is_verified=True),
    FeedItem("t2", "bob", "Just ate lunch", now - 600, likes=2),
    FeedItem("t3", "alice", "Thread on system design 🧵", now - 7200, likes=500, retweets=200, replies=50),
    FeedItem("t4", "news_bot", "Breaking: New tech release", now - 300, likes=1000, retweets=500, is_verified=True),
    FeedItem("t5", "carol", "Random thought", now - 1800, likes=5),
]

print("📱 Ranked Timeline for user1:")
for score, item in ranker.rank("user1", items):
    print(f"  [{score:.2f}] @{item.author_id}: {item.content} "
          f"(❤️{item.likes} 🔄{item.retweets})")
```

### Example 4: Notification System

```python
"""
Twitter notification system with fan-out and priority
"""
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List
import time
import uuid

class NotificationType(Enum):
    LIKE = "like"
    RETWEET = "retweet"
    REPLY = "reply"
    MENTION = "mention"
    FOLLOW = "follow"
    DM = "dm"

@dataclass
class Notification:
    notif_id: str
    user_id: str   # recipient
    actor_id: str   # who did the action
    notif_type: NotificationType
    content: str
    timestamp: float
    read: bool = False
    tweet_id: str = ""
    priority: int = 0  # Higher = more important

class NotificationService:
    """Handles notification generation, prioritization, delivery"""

    PRIORITY = {
        NotificationType.DM: 10,
        NotificationType.MENTION: 8,
        NotificationType.REPLY: 7,
        NotificationType.FOLLOW: 5,
        NotificationType.RETWEET: 3,
        NotificationType.LIKE: 1,
    }

    def __init__(self):
        self.notifications: Dict[str, List[Notification]] = defaultdict(list)
        self.preferences: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        self.unread_counts: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)

    def set_preferences(self, user_id: str, prefs: dict):
        self.preferences[user_id] = prefs

    def notify(self, user_id: str, actor_id: str,
               notif_type: NotificationType, content: str,
               tweet_id: str = ""):
        # Check preferences
        prefs = self.preferences.get(user_id, {})
        if prefs.get(f"mute_{notif_type.value}"):
            return None

        # Aggregate similar notifications (batch likes)
        if notif_type == NotificationType.LIKE and tweet_id:
            existing = self._find_aggregable(user_id, tweet_id, notif_type)
            if existing:
                existing.content = f"{actor_id} and others liked your tweet"
                existing.timestamp = time.time()
                return existing

        notif = Notification(
            notif_id=str(uuid.uuid4())[:8],
            user_id=user_id,
            actor_id=actor_id,
            notif_type=notif_type,
            content=content,
            timestamp=time.time(),
            tweet_id=tweet_id,
            priority=self.PRIORITY.get(notif_type, 0)
        )
        self.notifications[user_id].append(notif)
        self.unread_counts[user_id] += 1
        return notif

    def get_notifications(self, user_id: str, limit: int = 20,
                         unread_only: bool = False) -> List[Notification]:
        notifs = self.notifications.get(user_id, [])
        if unread_only:
            notifs = [n for n in notifs if not n.read]

        # Sort by priority then recency
        notifs.sort(key=lambda n: (n.priority, n.timestamp), reverse=True)
        return notifs[:limit]

    def mark_read(self, user_id: str, notif_ids: List[str] = None):
        if notif_ids is None:
            for n in self.notifications.get(user_id, []):
                n.read = True
            self.unread_counts[user_id] = 0
        else:
            for n in self.notifications.get(user_id, []):
                if n.notif_id in notif_ids:
                    n.read = True
                    self.unread_counts[user_id] = max(0, self.unread_counts[user_id] - 1)

    def _find_aggregable(self, user_id, tweet_id, notif_type):
        for n in self.notifications.get(user_id, []):
            if n.tweet_id == tweet_id and n.notif_type == notif_type and not n.read:
                return n
        return None

# ─── Demo ───
notif_svc = NotificationService()

# Multiple users like Alice's tweet
notif_svc.notify("alice", "bob", NotificationType.LIKE, "bob liked your tweet", "t1")
notif_svc.notify("alice", "carol", NotificationType.LIKE, "carol liked your tweet", "t1")
notif_svc.notify("alice", "dave", NotificationType.MENTION, "@alice check this out!", "t2")
notif_svc.notify("alice", "eve", NotificationType.FOLLOW, "eve followed you")
notif_svc.notify("alice", "frank", NotificationType.REPLY, "great post!", "t1")
notif_svc.notify("alice", "grace", NotificationType.DM, "Hey Alice, quick question")

print("🔔 Alice's notifications (sorted by priority):")
for n in notif_svc.get_notifications("alice"):
    icon = {"like": "❤️", "retweet": "🔄", "reply": "💬",
            "mention": "@", "follow": "👤", "dm": "✉️"}
    print(f"  {icon.get(n.notif_type.value, '•')} [{n.priority}] {n.content}")

print(f"\nUnread count: {notif_svc.unread_counts['alice']}")
```

### Example 5: Rate Limiter for Tweet API

```python
"""
Multi-tier rate limiter for Twitter API endpoints
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, Optional

@dataclass
class RateLimit:
    requests_per_window: int
    window_seconds: int

class SlidingWindowRateLimiter:
    """Sliding window rate limiter with multiple tiers"""

    # Twitter-like rate limits
    LIMITS = {
        "tweet_create": RateLimit(300, 3600),       # 300 tweets/hour
        "tweet_like": RateLimit(1000, 86400),        # 1000 likes/day
        "timeline_read": RateLimit(1500, 900),       # 1500 reads/15min
        "search": RateLimit(450, 900),               # 450 searches/15min
        "follow": RateLimit(400, 86400),             # 400 follows/day
        "dm_send": RateLimit(500, 86400),            # 500 DMs/day
    }

    def __init__(self):
        self.windows: Dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)

    def allow(self, user_id: str, action: str) -> dict:
        limit = self.LIMITS.get(action)
        if not limit:
            return {"allowed": True, "error": None}

        key = f"{user_id}:{action}"
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - limit.window_seconds

        # Remove expired entries
        self.windows[key] = [
            ts for ts in self.windows[key] if ts > window_start
        ]

        current_count = len(self.windows[key])
        remaining = limit.requests_per_window - current_count

        if current_count >= limit.requests_per_window:
            # Calculate retry-after
            oldest = min(self.windows[key]) if self.windows[key] else now
            retry_after = int(oldest + limit.window_seconds - now)
            return {
                "allowed": False,
                "remaining": 0,
                "limit": limit.requests_per_window,
                "retry_after": retry_after,
                "error": f"Rate limit exceeded for {action}"
            }

        self.windows[key].append(now)
        return {
            "allowed": True,
            "remaining": remaining - 1,
            "limit": limit.requests_per_window,
            "reset": int(window_start + limit.window_seconds),
        }

# ─── Demo ───
limiter = SlidingWindowRateLimiter()

# Simulate API calls
for i in range(5):
    result = limiter.allow("user1", "timeline_read")
    print(f"  Read {i+1}: allowed={result['allowed']}, remaining={result['remaining']}")

# Hit tweet limit
for i in range(302):
    result = limiter.allow("user1", "tweet_create")

print(f"\nAfter 302 tweet attempts: {result}")
```
